summary: addTargetHeader's bare `if (rootNodeId == null) return;` / `if (root == null) return;` (was tree_editing.dart:205-210) is gone. Both it and addNode now call a new _ensureRootNode(newNodes), which resolves / repairs / creates the container the insert hangs from and writes the id back onto the sequence's rootNodeId. Framing -> Add to Sequence -> Add target now actually adds the target on a rootless sequence instead of firing the disclosure snackbar that sent the user to the Sequencer, where the same insert failed the same way.

needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_editor/snippet_editing.dart has the same class of defect and is NOT in my ownership list. It is a `part` of the same library, so _ensureRootNode is directly callable from it. (a) line 49-50: `mergeParentId ??= _currentSequence!.rootNodeId; if (mergeParentId == null) return;` — merging a template snippet into a rootless sequence returns having written nothing, exactly as addTargetHeader used to. Should be `mergeParentId ??= _ensureRootNode(newNodes);`. (b) lines 154-160: when rootNodeId is null it mints an `InstructionSetNode(name: 'Sequence Root')`, uses it as the insert parent, but never writes its id onto the sequence's rootNodeId — so the snippet lands under a container nothing points at, invisible to rootNode/targetHeaders/the executor. Should be `insertParentId ??= _ensureRootNode(newNodes);` with `rootNodeId:` set on the closing copyWith.
caveats: Reachability of the rootless state was confirmed, not assumed: sequences.rootNodeId is `text().nullable()` (database/tables/sequences.dart:17), sequence_file_service.dart:241-247 only validates rootNodeId 'if present', sequences_dao.dart:267-268 falls back to the source id when the id-remap misses, and loadCopyForEditing (sequence_editor.dart:463) copies source.rootNodeId through verbatim — so a library row with a null root reaches the editor unchanged and Framing's picker hands it straight to addTargetHeader. The disclosure-only layer in add_target_to_sequence_flow.dart (read-back + 'Could not add' snackbar) was deliberately left in place: it still guards every other way the write could fail to land, and its test now proves it stays silent on this path.
